review_reference: UNSIGNED DRAFT: awaits the owner's signature of 0160 and 0161 and of runtime-grants.sql at the sha256s in files (numbers provisional, given at integration in release order: #258, 7168672285). APPT-1 Appointments with check-in to the waiting list (Release D, the department sprint the owner approved on 25 November 2026; hid-system#335), built at the recommended option of each open question, not yet answered by the owner: Q-APPT-1 A (check-in from an appointment opens the waiting-list row in the same transaction), Q-APPT-2 A (timed bookings with a server clash check, the clinician optional), Q-APPT-3 A (inbox, web push, email and the printable call list; SMS built but switched off), Q-APPT-4 A (staff book; the portal is read only), Q-APPT-5 A (who books), Q-APPT-6 A (an appointment is a check-in-only basis on its own day; Rahman's database check of 25 November answered A) and Q-APPT-7 A (the call list shows only the phone this facility recorded). ehr-api's and identity-api's APPOINTMENTS_ENABLED stay off in production until the clinical lead's checklist and the owner's go-live. Rahman's final database check of 63312e5f (#335, 25 November 20:51 UTC) found nothing blocking; this head carries his four should-fix points and the nits, as the coordinator decided on #258 (7174680244): 0160 takes identity.sealed_demo_members and identity.sealed_qa_members ACCESS SHARE NOWAIT up front (statement, both busy refusals, header, the suite's declared locks); runtime-grants.sql revokes ehr.appointment_events_sequence_no_seq from hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, and 0160 post-checks that the sequences its tables own carry no grant beyond the owner; post-checks in 0148's and 0152's form (the six tables and 27 functions owned by the owner of 0135's functions, row-level security enabled and not forced with no policy, the triggers by tgtype, tgqual, tgattr, tgnargs, tgfoid and tgenabled, and 0161 re-checks the control_key CHECK it rewrites); tolerant preconditions (the codes 0001-0151 give receptionist, doctor, clinician and nurse required as a subset, with no appointment code yet; a basis CHECK with other lanes' values after search and own_facility, rebuilt as search, own_facility, appointment and then those values); a BEFORE TRUNCATE guard on the appointment history; the not-forced row-level security stated as an exception in both headers; the runbook note that a role bootstrap after 0160 and 0161 uses the integration's runtime-grants.sql before the new images ship (docs/MIGRATION_RUNBOOK.md, Appointments). runtime-grants.sql is Release E's signed file (49b378f5..., signed 25 November 2026 with 0152 and 0153) byte for byte followed by the Appointments block. Releases after 0001-0153 (Release E, live since 25 November 2026 17:04 UTC at 0cfddcc9), before or after Billing (0162-0167) and Emergency (0168-0169). Rahman's re-check and the owner's signature are pending.
evidence: On throwaway PostgreSQL 16 databases (Docker, with pgvector) with fictional data only. Every build by the repo runner as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator; the role bootstrap and the suites run by the cluster superuser. The base: 0001-0153 (live 0cfddcc9's files) with Release E's runtime-grants.sql (49b378f5...), plus fictional staff (an active receptionist, doctor, clinician, nurse and lab member at one real facility), so 0160's closing count reaches rows as it does on production. Before the fixes, 63312e5f's 0160 and 0161 on that copy with runtime-grants.sql 732f7248...: appointments-migrations failed case 4h with 'identity.sealed_demo_members AccessShareLock, identity.sealed_qa_members AccessShareLock' (Rahman's finding reproduced); a dry run while another session held identity.sealed_qa_members failed after 5 s with 'canceling statement due to lock timeout', which the runner does not retry; after the bootstrap the history's sequence carried USAGE and SELECT for hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; and 0160 refused after Billing's 0162-0167 and after Emergency's 0168-0169 (the role table). With this head on the same copy: plan 2 pending at the sha256s in files, dry run rolled back, apply, plan 0 pending; the same dry run with identity.sealed_qa_members held gave 0160's busy refusal, was retried and succeeded; after the bootstrap the sequence carries no grant but its owner's. Suites: appointments-migrations 34 of 34 (also on a fresh build without the fictional staff, where the suite seeds its own membership), appointment-notices 70 of 70 (run outside the Lagos 07:00-21:00 reminder window), appointments 126 of 128. The two failing cases ('6 tomorrow's list at A, booked only' and '6 tomorrow, the clinic's') fail the same way with 63312e5f's suite on 63312e5f's files: the suite moves p1 to now plus 26 h 5 min, which after about 21:55 Lagos is the day after tomorrow (these runs were at about 22:30 Lagos). The new cases (the runtime cannot read or advance the sequence, no runtime role holds a privilege on it, TRUNCATE on the history is refused) fail on 63312e5f's build and pass here. Release order, each on a copy of the 0001-0153 base: Billing's 0162-0167 (6b253568), then 0160 and 0161: dry run, apply, 0 pending; Emergency's 0168-0169 (db83d733), then 0160 and 0161: dry run, apply, and the CHECK is search, own_facility, appointment, emergency (as 0168 leaves it after 0160); 0160 and 0161, then 0168-0169: applies; Billing and Emergency, then 0160 and 0161: applies; 0160 and 0161, then Billing's 0162: 0162 refuses on its own md5 pins of the shared roles (Billing's tolerant preconditions are that lane's fix). services/ehr-api db:test-staging-upgrade with HID_BASELINE_RUNTIME_GRANTS = Release E's file: passed (baseline 154, integrated 156, dry run rolled back, recorded checksums kept, migrator not superuser and without BYPASSRLS, 2,894 runtime privileges compared: a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql after the release changes none, sequences included; no row-level security or FORCE setting changed). Re-running Release E's runtime-grants.sql after 0160 and 0161 takes the EHR and Identity runtimes' EXECUTE on the appointment functions away and gives the sequence back (hence the runbook note). Release tests 123 of 126: 45, 53 and 100 fail only with 'missing migration prefix' (the provisional numbering gap 0154-0159); verify-migration-ledger accepts 0161 (156 files); build gates 70; scripts/tests 82 and 1 skipped; db:test-runner 15; ehr-api tsc clean, jest 23 (appointments and the 0136 count spec); identity-api 485 (the specs that read every migration, and appointments). Not run here: scripts/local-db-check.mjs (the full migration rehearsal with the live runtime verifiers and verify-appointments-runtime.mjs), which Rahman runs.
